**Belimarius Statue AC** 42; **Fort** +34, **Ref** +28, **Will** +37
**Belimarius Statue Hardness** 31; **HP** 120 (BT 60); **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **AC** 39, **Fort** +34, **Ref** +28, **Will** +37 **Runelord Statue Hardness** 29 **HP** 100 (BT 50); **HP** 120 (BT 60) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Covet Magic** **Trigger** A magic item or active spell effect enters the corridor; **Effect** A randomly determined statue uses the hazard’s [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2410) Magic action. The hazard then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (4 actions) The hazard uses Steal Magic twice. Once the implements of at least three runelord statues are charged, the hazard uses its next available action to Transfer Magic. If the hazard starts its turn with the Belimarius statue charged, the hazard uses its reaction to Empower Barrier. A disabled runelord statue can’t use Steal Magic. If the Belimarius statue is disabled, the hazard can’t use Transfer Magic or Empower Barrier.
**Steal Magic** [two-actions] Roll a d10 to determine which statue activates, rerolling a result of 10 or any result that would indicate a disabled statue or a statue that is already charged. The indicated statue casts _detonate magic_ with a +32 bonus to its counteract check. The spell targets the closest magic item within 120 feet, prioritizing the highest-ranking magic item and targeting spell effects only if no magic item is within range. On a success or critical success, the statue gathers the dispersed energy into its implement, charging it. While the statue’s implement remains charged, any creature who is at least an expert in Arcana, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) can use a 2-action activity with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to attempt a DC 44 check using that skill. On a success or critical success, they return the magic to its original source, causing it to reactivate. Removing an implement from its statue prevents the statue from using Transfer Magic but doesn’t prevent a creature from restoring the charge to its source.
**Transfer Magic** [one-action] **Requirements** The implements of at least three runelord statues are charged; **Effect** Three statues with charged implements transfer their charges to the Belimarius statue. While the Belimarius statue holds at least one charge, a creature can transfer charges from its implement as described in Steal Magic, except the DC of the skill check increases to DC 46; success returns the stolen magic to the appropriate items.
**Empower Barrier** [reaction] **Requirements** The hazard starts its turn, and the Belimarius statue holds at least one charge;
**Effect** The Belimarius statue transfers all charges from its implement into the force barrier separating the corridor from area **B3**. For every charge the statue transfers, the force barrier gains 10 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. (If the force barrier has been destroyed, the statue instead expends the first charge to cast a 6th-rank _wall of force_, with any remaining charges granting the barrier temporary Hit Points.) Charges transferred to the force barrier are lost forever and can’t be returned to items they were stolen from. --- **Reset** The hazard resets automatically if not disabled.

Meanwhile, the stairwell begins to collapse, starting from the top and working its way down. Any PC standing on the lower few steps falls into the pit unless they Grab the Edge with a successful DC 40 Reflex save. The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (2 actions) The haunt uses Leaden Limbs once, then Crumbling Stairs once.
**Leaden Limbs** [one-action] (arcane) The trap drains vigor from creatures in the stairwell, making their limbs feel as heavy as lead. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude saving throw with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 until the end of their next turn.
**Failure** The creature’s [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition value increases by 1, to a maximum of clumsy 4. The creature is slowed 1 as long as they remain clumsy. The clumsy condition ends as soon as the creature exits the stairwell.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the value increases by 2, and the creature is slowed 2.
**Crumbling Stairs** [one-action] A stretch of stairs crumbles, dropping into the void at the bottom of the stairwell. The first time the trap takes this action, the upper third of the stairwell collapses. The second time, the middle third collapses. The third time, the entire stairwell collapses. A creature on a collapsing section of stairs can try to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313) with a DC 40 Reflex save to avoid falling into the void. Flying creatures avoid the fall automatically but might tumble into the void anyway if their [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) condition prevents them from taking the Fly action on their turn. Though it appears to stretch forever, the void at the bottom of the stairwell functions as a portal to the Crypt of Sloth. Creatures who plummet into the void experience a fall that seems to take hours, but are eventually deposited in the middle of area **B10**, taking 80 bludgeoning damage from the fall. --- **Reset** The trap continues taking Leaden Limbs actions (and the void at the bottom of the stairwell remains open) for as long as creatures remain in the area. Once no creatures remain, the stairwell rebuilds itself, the void closes, and the trap resets.

**Success** The nightmare causes a momentary change to the creature’s appearance, causing its jaws to take on a frightening, fanged appearance and filling the creature’s mind with distracting, unsettling hunger that cause them to become [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of the nightmare feast’s next turn.
**Failure** The creature becomes [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) until the start of the nightmare feast’s next turn and gains a +30 bite (magical) that deals 3d12+10 slashing damage plus 2d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) on a hit. The creature favors this bite Strike when the confusion drives them to attack.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature also becomes [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) and can use the extra action to make bite Strikes. --- **Reset** The nightmare deactivates as soon as a round begins with no creatures in its area, and resets in 1d6 rounds.

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 79 **Complexity** Simple A trail of over-sized footprints crosses the path, markings of the apparently recent passage of a dangerous and mind-shattering entity whose stride is enough to be mistaken for depressions in the natural terrain, and promising destruction to those compelled to follow the tracks. --- **Stealth** DC 46 (master) **Disable** DC 46 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) (master) to distract those (including yourself) compelled to follow footprints, or DC 43 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) (legendary) to quickly obscure the trail **Beckoning Trail** (mental); **Trigger** A creature crosses over the footprints’ trail; **Effect** The triggering creature suddenly realizes the nature of the immense trail they just stepped into and feels a compulsion to follow the trail to their destination; the triggering creature must attempt a DC 35 Will save with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature Strides once down the trail before coming to their senses—this movement does not put the creature in any peril or danger.
**Success** The creature takes its three actions to Stride down the trail. While this movement doesn’t put the creature in any direct peril, when they end the movement, they’re overwhelmed with the knowledge that had they gone further, something horrible would have happened; the creature becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 hour by the close call.
**Failure** As success, but the creature becomes [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 and also stupefied 1 for 24 hours.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but doomed 2 and stupefied 2. In addition, at the end of the three Strides, the creature vanishes from view, instantly teleporting to some dangerous area or [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) prison. This might be a nearby location that the creature’s allies can discover and rescue them from, or it may be somewhere further away that will require more effort to reach before the victim can be rescued. --- **Reset** The unspeakable impressions fade once they are triggered, but reform somewhere else in the vicinity 24 hours later unless they are successfully disabled.
